//: AI skill by level (0 = beginner, 1 = the top difficulty, tuned against professional match statistics: tools/match-stats.ts, docs/ai.md). Each list holds the value at evenly spaced levels from 0 to 1 ([level 0, level 0.5, level 1]), interpolated linearly between. timing: SD of the release error in seconds against the game's timing windows (the same windows humans are judged on). motor: the swing-to-swing spread that is not timing (data/shots.json swing.motor per unit). pressure: how much the motor spread grows per unit of pressure (src/sim/ai/pressure.ts): a hard, fast, stretched or low ball is played less steadily. smashEffort: the fraction of the smash shape's full face speed (shots.json racketMax, with the power modifier) an AI swings at (ShotRequest.power). In play, semi-professionals smash at 120.7 +- 9.8 km/h against opponents (133.1 unopposed) and amateurs at 104.5 (124.6) (Rivilla-Garcia et al. 2019, radar); highly trained men smash fed lobs at about 133 km/h (Saez de Villarreal et al. 2023). Fitted so the in-play median is about 105-110 km/h at level 0 and 125-133 at level 1 (tools/match-stats.ts); a human's smash stays at full effort. chaseEffort: the fraction of the top speed (that way) an AI runs at for the ball when the time left doesn't ask for more (it still goes flat out when it must). Flat out every time, every AI player hit the cap (4.8-5.0 m/s sideways) within ten minutes, against a median per-match top speed of 4.2 m/s for WPT men (Miralles et al. 2025, WIMU GNSS + LPS, a smoothed signal over 85-minute matches); fitted so the 0.5 s-smoothed per-match peak is about 4.2-4.5 m/s. glassWait: Player.glassWait for an AI, how strongly the planner waits for a deep ball to come off the back glass (a human's is 1, the owner's wall play); at 1 the AI played 27% of its shots off the back glass against 12.8% for WPT men (2014), at 0 21% (REVIEW.md round 1). bajada: the chance by level that a ball coming off our own back glass high is taken as a bajada (an overhead off the glass), fitted so the top level plays one in 15% of points (WPT men 2020: 14-17%, Courel-Ibáñez et al. 2024); it was 0.25 at level 1 until net players took deep lobs in the air (review round 2), which left fewer lobs to come off the glass: the top level now takes nearly every one it can. ohArrive: Player.ohArrive for an AI, the speed (m/s) an overhead may still be moving at when it is met: players take a deep lob's bandeja or smash still drifting back (the scissor kick of a smash is struck going backwards), and the shot's moving error (data/shots.json swing) pays for it; an estimate (no published speed at contact), at 0 every overhead had to stop first, and lobs a step deep went to the glass. pressure was 1.15 and motor at level 1 0.65 until round 1: forced errors were 24% of endings against the pros' 29-33% and unforced 35%.

women.//: How a women's match differs from a men's (review round 5, the pro's #5; docs/review/round5-pro.md has the sources). speed: top running speed against the men's (14.1 against 15.2 km/h). smash: how much of an overhead is a smash against the men's (17% of overheads against 26.6%). smashEffort: how hard against the men's, fitted to how points end (no published speed). lob: how often against the men's. serveGlass, serveT: first serves to the glass and the T (T 30.3%, middle 7.3%). serveEdge: how far inside the line a first serve aims, in serve-box steps against the men's 0.85 (first serves in 87.7% against 92.9%). serveEffort: how hard against the men's, fitted with smashEffort. At these values, 2000 points: winners 73 / 17 / 4 by double bounce, came back, out (published 76.9 / 11.8 / 11.3), first serves in 89.5 (87.7), but the serving pair still wins 58 (published 48.5).
